name: Shillem
overview: Shillem was a male member of the tribe of Naphtali, identified as a son of Naphtali. He is noted in Scripture as part of the list of the "sons of Israel" who journeyed to Egypt, marking his inclusion in the foundational genealogies of Israel. His descendants, known as the Shillemites, are also mentioned in the wilderness census, linking him to the continued identity of the Naphtali tribe.
namesAndTitles: The name Shillem means "recompense" and possibly also "whole, healthy, complete," reflecting themes of restoration or wholeness. This proper name is recorded in Genesis 46:24 and is not indicated as given directly by God. Another related name, Shallum, means "peace, well-being, prosperity," though it refers to a different individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shillem as a son of Naphtali, establishing his place in the tribal lineage of Israel. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shillem's significance lies in his role as an ancestor within the tribe of Naphtali, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. His mention among those who moved to Egypt situates him within the narrative of Israel's descent into Egypt, a pivotal moment leading to the Exodus. The identification of the Shillemites in the wilderness census further underscores his lasting legacy in the formation and organization of the Israelite community during their journey to the Promised Land.
